2. Angelicus 29 [C. 4, 8]. — Chartac., cm. 22 × 14,5, ff. VI + 346, multa inter-
ciderunt cf. infra ad f. 173, 187, 207. Codicem scripserunt tres librarii : 1o fere totum
codicem exaravit a. 1388 Eleutherius Eleus (cf. f. 152r), qui et anno 1390 codi-
cem Taurinensem 4 descripsit (Catal. ital., p. 5), cf. n. ad f. 152v; altera s. XV,
ff. scripsit 209-212v, 305-346v; tertia s. XV, supplevit ff. 137-148v. — Insunt et in
margine adnotationes quaedam : Summo margine folii 1r κτῆμα Γεωργ<ίου>
κόμητος τοῦ κορινθίου; infra repetita sunt eadem et * Astrologia „ manu Philippi
Vitalis. F. 10r summo marg. παναγία τριὰς βοήθει μοι τῷ σῷ λάτρει ἐλευθερίῳ †;
imo marg. sigill. Biblioth. Passioneae etc. Cf. descriptionem Georgii Muccio in
Studi italiani di filologia classica, IV, p. 64. — Praestantissimus hic codex solus
Apomasaris et Palchi opera nobis servasse videtur. Ex eo fluxerunt codd. Lau-
rent. 28, 33 [= Flor. 11], Ambrosianus B, 38 sup. [= Mediol. 8], Vaticanus 1057
[v. infra] etc. Itaque accuratissime hunc archetypum descripsimus etsi plura iam

sections.en: 2. Angelicus 29 [C. 4, 8]. — Paper, 22 × 14.5 cm, ff. VI + 346, many have fallen out cf. below at f. 173, 187, 207. Three scribes wrote the codex: the 1st wrote almost the whole codex in the year 1388, Eleutherius Eleus (cf. f. 152r), who also in the year 1390 copied the codex Taurinensis 4 (Catal. ital., p. 5), cf. note to f. 152v; the second of the 15th c., wrote ff. 209-212v, 305-346v; the third of the 15th c., supplied ff. 137-148v. — There are also some annotations in the margin: In the top margin of folio 1r 'possession of George count of Corinth'; below the same are repeated and 'Astrologia' in the hand of Philippus Vitalis. F. 10r top margin 'Holy Trinity help me your servant Eleutherius †'; bottom margin seal of the Bibliotheca Passionea etc. Cf. the description by Georgius Muccio in Studi italiani di filologia classica, IV, p. 64. — This most excellent codex alone seems to have preserved for us the works of Apomasar and Palchus. From it flowed codd. Laurent. 28, 33 [= Flor. 11], Ambrosianus B, 38 sup. [= Mediol. 8], Vaticanus 1057 [see below] etc. Therefore we have described this archetype most accurately even if many things have already been reviewed in Catal., I, when we were dealing with its copy, cod. Flor. 11.

summary.headline: Astrological Judgments and Hermes
summary.text: Catalog entries for Angelicus 29, folios 335–339, covering astrological judgments on children, marriage, crafts, speech, renting, wine decanting, diurnal and vocal signs, stellar friendship and enmity, the nature of the twelve signs, and Mars’s March ingress. The final folios transmit Hermes the philosopher’s letter to Ammon the Egyptian, followed by notes on measures and medical works; the apparatus identifies the codex’s scribes, marginalia, Apomasar and Palchus texts, and related manuscript witnesses.
